strengths: Systematic, principled approach using EASI taxonomy for decomposing spatial intelligence into core capabilities
Large-scale curated dataset (8M samples) with sophisticated filtering and image selection pipeline
Strong empirical results across 5 diverse benchmarks, surpassing GPT-5 on perspective-taking (80.7% vs lower performance)
Rigorous robustness evaluation including circular tests, VSI-Debiased evaluation, and no-vision controls demonstrating genuine visual grounding
Comprehensive analysis of scaling behaviors, emergent generalization, and single-dataset training necessity
Multi-architecture validation (InternVL3, Qwen3-VL, Bagel) demonstrating approach generalization
Public commitment to release models, code, and dataset, providing significant community value
Downstream validation on embodied AI without finetuning (+59.6% success rate improvement)
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty—primarily data-centric scaling without architectural innovation or modifications to base models
Preliminary and inconclusive CoT analysis showing only 2-7% gains; proposed hypotheses are speculative rather than conclusive
Saturation plateau effects (Fig 1) suggest fundamental limitations of scaling-only approaches; paper acknowledges but doesn't address paradigm shift needed
Synthetic data quality control procedures underspecified: validation methodology, error rates, and manual verification extent not reported for 4.5M generated samples
Data contamination prevention not explicitly discussed despite combining diverse multi-source datasets; risk of train-test overlap unclear
Limited failure mode analysis—Section 5.7 shows failures but provides no systematic breakdown or generalizable insights
Generalization concerns: predominantly indoor scene training (ScanNet-based); modest SITE performance (47.7%) suggests distribution specificity
Training setup inadequately justified: single-epoch training rationale unexplained, learning rate arbitrary (5×10⁻⁶), no statistical significance testing or error bars reported
Missing ablations on dataset composition, data mixture sensitivity, and impact of individual spatial capabilities
Dense presentation (33 pages) with normalized radar charts obscuring absolute performance differences; CoT notation inconsistently applied
